problem: Prior egocentric navigation work (EgoNav, EgoCast, COPILOT) assumes static environments and ignores active information-gathering head turns. VLN and robot social navigation target wheeled or legged robots in simulation and do not match the human/humanoid form factor. Real-world egocentric human navigation data with dynamic obstacles is also scarce.
motivation: Deployable humanoid, VR/AR and assistive navigation need collision-free short-horizon trajectories around pedestrians and vehicles from egocentric video. Humans turn their heads to gather information, for example checking traffic before crossing, and this matters given the camera's limited FoV. Collecting such data at scale is hard because humanoid robots are hard to deploy in the real world.
key_idea: Predict future 6D head poses (translation and rotation) from a posed monocular egocentric video by unprojecting per-frame DINOv2 features into a 3D volume, average-pooling it over time, and regressing the poses from a BEV network. The model is trained on a new Aria-glasses dataset of real-world navigation.
insight: The ablations show DINO semantics are the most important ingredient: without DINO, L1_trans rises from 0.17 to 0.35 and L1_rot from 0.16 to 0.67. Pooling in 2D only, without the 3D unprojection, also hurts (0.26/0.44). BEV projection matches 3D convolution (0.17/0.19) at lower cost. Adding depth improves dynamic-obstacle avoidance, since the SLAM point cloud contains only static structure. The A* baseline avoids static obstacles almost perfectly but fails on dynamic ones, which shows that dynamic obstacles need learned semantic perception.
method: DINO encoding: a frozen dinov2_vits14_reg encoder on 224x224 frames gives 16x16x384 feature maps per frame.

Parameter-free unprojection: a 96x32x96 voxel grid in a head-centered, gravity-aligned canonical frame is projected into each frame's pixels. Features are bilinearly sampled, then average-pooled over the T1=8 frames into a 3D volume.
BEV projection: an MLP squeezes the Y axis (384*Y -> 384 channels) to give a Z x X x 384 BEV map.
BEV Net: 11 modules (Conv2D + LayerNorm + MLP/GELU), with hidden dimension growing from 384 to 1540 and spatial size reduced to 3x3.
Trajectory head: spatial average pooling followed by a 3-layer MLP that outputs 8 future 6D poses (translation plus 6D rotation representation). The loss is L1 on translation and rotation.

AND dataset pipeline: Project Aria glasses record RGB, SLAM, eye tracking, IMU and GPS at 20 fps. Aria MPS provides head poses and point clouds. Data are cut into 16-step clips with stride and dilation 6 (4.5 s), and faces are blurred with EgoBlur.
Optional extensions: goal position concatenated to the final MLP; depth or point-cloud occupancy voxels concatenated to the 3D volume.

setting.backbone: Frozen DINOv2 ViT-S/14 (reg) encoder + BEV convnet/MLP trained from scratch
setting.training_data: Aria Navigation Dataset (AND): about 4 h, 274k RGB frames, 36k clips, 18 locations, collected by the authors; the training split is disjoint from held-out unseen environments
setting.observation: Posed monocular egocentric RGB video (8 past frames with 6D head poses); no depth or LiDAR in the main model
setting.action_space: Predicted future 6D head pose sequence (8 steps, translation + rotation); not a discrete or low-level action space
setting.simulator: real world only (offline evaluation on recorded data)
setting.privileged: none at test time (poses come from Aria SLAM; the goal is used only in the '+goal' variant; GT point cloud is used only for evaluation metrics)

numbers.eval_set_note: held-out set of environments unseen during training

numbers.extra: GT final-step head translation given as goal input
additional depth input converted to occupancy voxels

numbers_note: Results are on the authors' own new dataset, not a standard navigation benchmark; the split is a held-out unseen-environment set, labeled 'val' here. Metrics are offline (no closed-loop success).
results: On held-out environments, the model beats the adapted EgoCast (L1_trans 0.34 -> 0.17, L1_rot 0.63 -> 0.16) and the constant-velocity and linear-extrapolation baselines on all metrics. It also improves both static and dynamic non-collision scores (e.g. Col_dyn_25 90.3 vs 86.2). With a goal, A*+Lin_Ext has near-perfect static non-collision but poor dynamic scores, while the goal-conditioned model is better overall on trajectory error.
limitations: A deterministic regression head cannot model multimodal futures and regresses to the mean, for example when the person could go left or right around a pedestrian.
Rare scenarios absent from the 4 h training set, such as rails requiring a look-down, are not handled.
Evaluation is offline with proxy non-collision metrics (depth-estimated distances to people, SLAM point clouds); there is no closed-loop or real-robot deployment.
